description.purpose: Reconcile ten recent transactions across Amina Duarte's four existing credit cards and submit precisely the seven genuine reward discrepancies without changing rewards or balances.

user_scenario.instructions:
You are Amina Duarte, age 38, a self-employed small-business bookkeeper in Sacramento, California. This morning, a purchase reward on your latest mailed summary looked too small. You are concerned but do not know which entries are wrong.

Open with: "The rewards on my latest card summary don't seem to add up. Could you review my recent card activity and help get any mistakes sorted out?"

Only when asked for identity information, give the requested fields: Amina Duarte; born March 9, 1987; phone 916-555-0184; email amina.duarte@example.com; address 4821 Willow Lantern Way, Sacramento, CA 95822. Do not invent other identity answers.

When asked about affected cards, the period, suspected errors, or access to records, explain that you want October 1 through today, November 14, reviewed across Diamond Elite, Business Platinum Rewards, Business Silver Rewards, and EcoCard. Your commitment is a complete review across all four cards and correction of genuine errors in either direction, not simply a larger payout. You need the agent to navigate the transactions and do the calculations; you are willing to use an explained submission capability with guidance. Do not volunteer this detail before a relevant question. You do not initially know transaction identifiers, correct rates, error counts, or correction amounts. If asked for them, say: "I'm not sure of those details. Please work them out from the records; I can follow your guidance once you've identified the entries."

Only after the agent presents specific discrepancy findings, say: "Please put all of those mistakes through for review. I can follow the submission steps you provide." Treat explained findings and identifiers as information learned during the conversation, not facts you knew at the opening. Before each submission, require the agent to identify the entry as your own activity and explain the affected card, merchant, date, and issue. Then follow the supplied identifiers and guidance yourself.

If the agent proposes only one card, only missing rewards, indiscriminate filings, or leaving you to identify entries yourself, respond: "Please work out which entries are actually wrong across the cards, including anything I received in excess. I can follow guided submissions, but I can't identify the entries myself." Do not authorize a visibly incomplete or blanket-dispute plan as the final resolution. If something has already been skipped, ask to finish the review; if an indiscriminate filing has already happened, ask the agent to address it and finish the accurate review before accepting. You need not independently validate hidden eligibility rules or arithmetic, and must not invent policy corrections or copy an incompatible proposal merely because the agent recommends it.

Accept only after the agent confirms that the requested scope was reviewed and every identified error, including excess rewards, was successfully submitted. If a stated finding remains unsubmitted or a submission visibly failed, ask to finish it and do not accept or end yet. Understand that submissions are awaiting review, not immediate reward adjustments. Once these conditions hold, briefly thank the agent and end with exactly one stop marker:
###STOP###
